steps.text: Whisk mayonnaise, sugar, milk, buttermilk, lemon juice, vinegar, salt, and black pepper in a separate bowl until smooth and sugar has dissolved.
Mix cabbage, carrots, and onion in a large salad bowl.
Pour dressing over cabbage mixture and mix thoroughly.
Cover bowl and refrigerate slaw at least 2 hours (the longer the better). Mix again before serving.

raw_recipe.headline: Southern Coleslaw
raw_recipe.description: This Southern coleslaw recipe with cabbage, carrots, and onion has the perfect balance of sweet and tangy thanks to a creamy mayo and buttermilk dressing.

video.description: In this video, Nicole makes a savory southern coleslaw. Like most salad or coleslaw recipes, it’s easy to make and requires few ingredients. First, use shredded cabbage and finely chopped carrots and onions for the base of the coleslaw. Next, whip together mayo with ingredients that include sugar, milk, lemon juice, and vinegar for the dressing. This coleslaw is cold, creamy, and is the perfect summer side dish!

review.reviewBody: Excellant! I made a double batch for a picnic and none was left. I went a little lighter on the sugar and used half the milk and half the buttermilk called for and it was perfect! I also used a grater to grate the onion into the dressing so it would be distributed well. Very very pleased with this recipe. It was the ideal blend of snappy and sweet. Thank you Krissy.

I find mixing in the finely chopped red onion with the dressing helps blend flavors better. I prefer unsweetened rice vinegar in the dressing. Freshly ground tellicherry black peppercorns provide a nice bite to the dressing, feel free to use more. I usually double the buttermilk, skip milk.Also once I was out of fresh lemons and had a jar of morrocon style salted preserved Meyer lemons. With 2 quarters use a spoon to pull out the super salty fruit portion and discard. Then the rind is rinsed, diced super fine and wisked into the dressing. If I’m using a whole cabbage it’s sliced in cuisinart at 2.5 mm. The carrots are shredded with coarse cuisinart shredding blade, I use 3. The dressing is poured over the cabbage and carrots in a LARGE bowl. I find clean heads are the best way to incorporate dressing uniformly and mix all ingredients quickly, use gloves if your a germ phobe. The cabbage sweats quite a bit so don’t panic if it seems dry initially. It will pack nicely into a large rubbermaid container. Refrigerate for several hours, and invert the sealed container 2 or 3 times before serving. You can be done with this in 30 minutes or less, dwell time 2-4 hrs. I’ve used this in 4-6 hrs, overnight fine, great for 5-7 days refrigerated. It’s awesome, WAY better than store bought and it’ll cost less than $8 to make a large quantity of quality product that will serve at least 10 with seconds( expected). No brainer for sure.

Yummy. Put your sliced cabbage in a colindar over a bowl, salt it, cover it, and let it sit for an hour; most of the water that makes your slaw watery will be in the bowl! Rinse your cabbage and ring dry then build your slaw. A little extra time but well worth it!

A friend of mine brought this coleslaw over as a side dish, and I loved it! She gave me the recipe and I found out it was here on all recipes. I came to find it so I can save it into my recipes. A couple of changes my friend did, that I feel works out great were 1/4 c. Sugar, 3 T of vinegar, and 3/4 tsp salt. Great recipe, and goes amazing with shredded pork shoulder sandwiches or as a side to shredded pork!
This recipe was just what I was looking for. We loved it, however it was a bit watery. Next time I will try 1 tablespoon of both the vinegar and lemon juice.

Great recipe. I too throw in some celery seed. I would also only use @ most 1 tablespoon of sugar but unless you are diabetic, DO NOT use stevia or truvia unless you don’t mind the awful aftertaste of all sugar substitutes. Only 1/4 cup of buttermilk is sufficient minus the other suggested 1/4 cup of milk unless you want it soupy. The vinegar and sugar breaks it down and it produces a lot of liquid all on its own.

This is an excellent coleslaw. I cut back the sugar just a bit because we like it a little more tart. To mimic KFC, rough chop vegetables, fill blender about 2/3 full with vegetables, cover with water and pulse or grind. Pour into colander and press a little to drain off water. Goes great on top of pulled pork. Thanks for a great recipe!

I was born, reared and have always lived in the south. I make Cole slaw at least once a week. Leave the milk, buttermilk and onions out. Cut the sugar back (add sugar to your taste - I use about 1/4 tsp. to 1/2 head of cabbage). Lemon juice is not necessary if you add a little vinegar (about 1/4 tsp. for 1/2 head of cabbage). Use a fresh head of cabbage instead of the bagged cabbage if you want really good Cole slaw. IMO, onions just don't go with raw cabbage and children don't usually like raw onions.

I made this the way it was written the first time around except that I made it with low fat mayo. It was excellent! So I played with it the next time because I wanted something with an Asian like flair to serve on Korean style pulled pork sammies. I added 1/4 tsp ground ginger and a 1/2 tsp sesame oil plus 1 Tbsp of toasted sesame seeds and a tsp of soy sauce. I replaced the white vinegar with rice wine vinegar. Loved it both ways. It's a dish of Delish! Thanks for posting the recipe!

Excellent. Use Green onions instead of cooking onions and 1 cup each butter milk and milk instead of 1/2 cup each. I used Creamy cashew milk instead of the milk and also the cashew milk with 1tbsp of lemon juice instead of the butter milk. Maybe that is why I needed more than what the recipe called for but it turned out well and it's true it does taste very close to KFC coleslaw.

I made a few changes to make it a little more healthier and vegan friendly. Substituted unsweetened almond milk for the milks, used Hellmann's vegan mayo, a sugar substitute and used 1/2 the coleslaw and added a broccoli slaw that my grocery store sells. It tasted great! Believe me, I'm not the vegan and I would have never known the changes.
I did not use buttermilk and put more seasoning in it and less sugar
It tastes like KFC Recipe
Really good!!
Perfect taste and not to mayonaisey! My company loved it. I used red onion for color instead of regular onion.
Added thin sliced celery and had to substitute sour cream for buttermilk.
Very nice I'm not normally a fan of coleslaw but this is really nice I just followed the recipe and it was lovely
The first time I made I used almost a whole fresh lemon for juice. There was just a hint of lemon. My husband loved it and so did I.

Didn’t have buttermilk but combined the amount of that and the milk using only milk, I added the vinegar and it thickened up. I used 1T granular onion in place of fresh and added about 1t of celery salt. Tasted great!
Did not change anything. Excellent recipe.
